title: Circular Analyses Helper Functions
text: circhelp small helper package circular data analyses R, particularly useful cognitive studies orientation, motion direction, circular features. package contains functions descriptive statistics circular data (computing means, SD, skewness), angular differences, correlation. also includes function correct cardinal biases human estimates circular features (e.g., orientation). documentation available package help files https://achetverikov.github.io/circhelp/.

code: library(ggplot2) p <- ggplot(Pascucci_et_al_2019_data, aes(x = orientation, y = err)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.05) +   labs(x = "Orientation, deg.", y = "Error, deg.") p1 <- p + geom_smooth(method = "loess") + ggtitle("Standard LOESS") p2 <- p + geom_smooth(method = "circ_loess", method.args = list(circ_space = 180, span = 0.5)) +   ggtitle("Circular LOESS, span = 0.5") p3 <- p + geom_smooth(method = "circ_loess", method.args = list(circ_space = 180, span = 0.2)) +   ggtitle("Circular LOESS, span = 0.2") (p1 + p2 + p3) #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x' #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x' #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

title: circhelp: Circular Analyses Helper Functions — circhelp-package
text: Light-weight functions computing descriptive statistics different circular spaces (e.g., 2pi, 180, 360 degrees), handle angle-dependent biases, pad circular data, . Specifically aimed psychologists neuroscientists analyzing circular data. text: dt data.table data. circ_space Circular space, can 180 360 (default: 180). weights_sd Standard deviation Gaussian window use across xvar (default: 10). kernel_bw Bandwidth kernel density estimator across yvar. NULL, computed using stats::bw.SJ(). "average", computed using stats::bw.SJ() group indicated averaged. Otherwise passed stats::density() (default: NULL). xvar X-axis variable, dissimilarity items (default: "abs_td_dist"). yvar Y-axis variable, normally errors (default: "bias_to_distr_corr"). vector grouping variable names (default: empty vector). n number steps x-axis variable density computed (default: 181). average TRUE, asymmetry averaged x-value (default: TRUE). return_full_density TRUE, returns full data.table density computed point (default: FALSE). normalize TRUE, normalizes difference probability density total sum probability density (zero point excluded). Delta corresponds probability observing given sign. use average TRUE. wrap TRUE (default), kernel density estimate wrapped around circle, kernel centred near one end yvar axis reappears end instead truncated. Set FALSE pre-1.4.0 (truncated) behaviour. orientation colour data, errors sit near zero bandwidth degrees, changes nothing ~1e-13; matters yvar carries mass near +/- circ_space/2, 180-degrees-reversals motion-direction data. exclude_antipode TRUE (default), +/- circ_space/2 point dropped positive negative sums, exactly like zero. angle approached two sides sign, n odd otherwise counted twice (-max_diss +max_diss). Set FALSE pre-1.4.0 behaviour. n_wraps Number periodic images summed side wrap TRUE (default: 1). One already far past double precision bandwidth much smaller circ_space. rescale_narrow TRUE (default), bandwidth narrower spacing x_grid triggers rescaling yvar bandwidth common factor, kernel least one grid cell wide. asymmetry signed mass difference positive scaling preserves value's sign, estimand unchanged; equivalent evaluating finer grid, cheaper. Without , kernel narrower cell falls grid points rectangle sum stops representing density (kernel_bw = dx/20 point centred cell contributes 7.98x mass one half cell away contributes 0). stats::bw.SJ() reach regime real data. Set FALSE pre-1.4.0 behaviour. scale_safety Fraction circ_space/2 rescaled yvar values allowed reach (default: 0.5). Rescaling treats circular axis linear, valid mass near wrap, factor capped rather assumed safe.

title: Weighted standard error of the mean (SEM_w) — weighted_sem
text: James Kirchner describes two different cases weighted variance computed. code implements Case "one wants give weight points others, considered important" "weights differ uncertainties associated individual xi assumed " (Kirchner, 2006, p. 1). formula used : \[SEM_w = \sqrt{\left(\sum_{= 1}^{N} (w_{} x_i^2)-\bar{x}^2\right)\frac{\sum_{= 1}^{N} w_i^2}{1-\sum_{= 1}^{N} w_i^2}} \] expected error within 5% bootstrapped SEM (larger sample sizes).

title: circhelp 1.4.0
text: density_asymmetry(): kernel density estimate now wrapped around circle (wrap = TRUE), mass near +/- circ_space/2 longer truncated. -op ~1e-13 orientation colour errors, matters data 180-degrees-reversal mode, motion direction. density_asymmetry(): +/- circ_space/2 point now excluded positive negative sums (exclude_antipode = TRUE), like zero. angle reached two sides, odd n counted twice. density_asymmetry(): bandwidth narrower grid spacing now rescales yvar bandwidth together (rescale_narrow = TRUE) kernel spans least one cell. Without , rectangle sum aliases: narrow error distribution bw.SJ()-selected bandwidth returned asymmetry 7.5% value default n = 181, now 0.4%. density_asymmetry(): two signs now paired rounded abs(x), since seq() bitwise symmetric every n (n = 1801, 604 900 pairs failed match dropped sums entirely). density_asymmetry_discrete(): four fixes, argument names defaults. Wrapping done evaluating stats::density() neighbouring periods folding images back, since augmenting sample shifted copies run density()’s binning range. fixes default corrected behaviour; pass wrap = FALSE, exclude_antipode = FALSE, rescale_narrow = FALSE pre-1.4.0 results.
